data.body:
Root-cause investigation complete; remediation in progress on branch `fix-a11a-redispatch`.

## Outcome: proximate mechanism CONFIRMED, ultimate trigger NOT reproduced

Followed the 4-phase debugging protocol. Phase 2 (compare against working
examples) was the step that produced the result.

**The discriminating difference.** Of the seven tests driving this workflow step,
this is the ONLY one whose verdict depends on `dispatch_out` being intact AND on
the match succeeding. The two sibling failure tests stub `gh` to write to stderr
only and assert a NON-zero exit, so they pass identically whether the match logic
works or fails — they are structurally blind to this defect. The happy-path and
pacing tests never reach the match at all. That is why one test failed alone.

**Confirmed mechanism.** The verdict was decided by

    printf '%s' "$dispatch_out" | grep -q 'HTTP 422' \
      && printf '%s' "$dispatch_out" | grep -qi 'disabled workflow'

Shadowing `grep` with one that always exits 1 reproduces the CI failure
BYTE-FOR-BYTE: same three captured lines, same `::error::` branch, same
`assert 1 == 0`. So the observed CI output is exactly what a non-zero return from
that pipeline produces — which reconciles the contradiction that `dispatch_out`
demonstrably carried both tokens while the fatal branch ran.

**What remains unverified:** what made that pipeline return non-zero on that one
runner. Not reproduced, and I am not claiming it. Eliminated by experiment:

- `pipefail` + `grep -q` SIGPIPE race — 500 pipeline trials, 1,500 whole-script
  trials and 5,000 two-stream capture trials on Linux under CPU contention, fork
  churn and a 512 MB cap: zero failures, zero lost or reordered output. Also
  mechanically impossible for a ~100-byte payload.
- A stale or mutated workflow file — no test and no CI lane writes it.
- Runner resource exhaustion — no OOM, fork-retry, ENOSPC or `Text file busy` in
  the run log.
- Leaked process-wide state inheritable by the child (`setrlimit`, `umask`,
  signal dispositions) — every occurrence in the suite restores in a `finally`,
  and none touches SIGPIPE.

Three hypotheses refuted is the protocol's escalation point, so I stopped hunting
the trigger and fixed the class instead.

## Fix

The verdict is now computed with shell BUILTINS (`[[ == ]]`, with `nocasematch`
scoped to the phrase so the status stays an exact match). No second process can
return non-zero into it, so the trigger — whatever it was — is now unreachable.
Narrowness is preserved: both tokens still required, every other failure still
fatal.

New oracle `test_redispatch_downgrade_survives_a_failing_external_command` pins
the property by shadowing `grep` with `exit 1`. Verified RED on the pre-fix
workflow and GREEN after, with the three sibling tests unchanged and passing.
`make lint` (incl. zizmor + actionlint on the modified workflow) is clean;
`make verify` running.
